body:
support_jamie: FYI escalating a customer-reported streaming issue (alexa-app). They get an initial assistant chunk immediately, then ~20–40s of silence, then a final small chunk. Happening ~30% of requests. Customer provided request IDs below. Need repro steps + what logs/pcap to collect.

support_tina: Thanks Jamie — can you paste the request IDs, region, and whether they're using HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 or a proxy (CF/NGINX) in front?

support_jamie: req ids: req_9a3f2c, req_9a3f9d, trace: trc-78b4. Customer in us-west1, fronted by a Cloudflare worker -> origin to our edge uses HTTP/2. They said Chrome + Node fetch both show same behavior.

customer_alexa: confirming: client = chrome + fetch() and a Node service that proxies to our API. Symptoms: first assistant chunk arrives (tokens ~0–20), then nothing for ~30s, then one final small chunk with the remaining tokens. No 5xx. Latency on the API call shows normal tail time but interleaved chunks missing.

eng_runtime_lee: Helpful context — this sounds like interleaving/coalescing on the connection path or our keepalive/flush interaction. Two immediate asks: 1) Can you get a raw streaming capture (curl -v with --no-buffer) from the customer that hits our API directly (no worker) and one that goes via the worker? 2) Grab the full request/response headers and the per-chunk timing (timestamps).

eng_sre_maya: Also request: if customer can run a tcpdump or ngrep against the proxy -> origin connection that would rule in/out proxy coalescing. Eg: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/stream.pcap host <redwood-edge-ip> and port 443` (they can redact keys). If they can't share pcap, we need the edge trace IDs and our ingress logs (we'll fetch once we have exact request_ts).

devex_ravi: Repro curl I usually give customers — include Accept header + http1.1 + no-buffer:

```bash
curl -v -N \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  --http1.1 \n  --no-buffer \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-test","input":"say hello and stream tokens slowly"}' \n  "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat/stream"
```

devex_ravi: `-N` + `--no-buffer` + `--http1.1` forces unbuffered SSE on many client stacks; ask them to run that against our endpoint and paste raw binary output (or upload to pastebin).

customer_alexa: ran the curl directly to our backend (bypassing worker) and saw continuous streaming (no long silence). Ran through worker and the silence reproduces. Posted small sample of raw output (redacted):

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream

data: {"role":"assistant","delta":"Hello,\n"}

# ~30s silence

data: {"role":"assistant","delta":"...rest of output"}
```

eng_runtime_lee: That strongly points to the worker/proxy coalescing or buffering SSE until certain thresholds. Cloudflare has HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 translation and may buffer small frames. Two useful checks: 1) Does the worker set `Connection: keep-alive` vs `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`? 2) Are there any content-length headers overwritten?

eng_sre_maya: For our logs, if you can provide the exact request timestamp (ISO) and the req_id we can pull the ingress logs and the upstream tcp timings. Please also run this curl from the worker origin environment (if they can run a small curl from the worker or an origin server) capturing timing: `curl -w "%{time_total} %{time_starttransfer}" -o /dev/null -s ...`

support_tina: Customer attached the worker script snippet — they do `fetch(apiUrl, {headers, method: 'POST', body})` then `return new Response(res.body)` (no special streaming transforms).

eng_runtime_lee: That pattern should stream but if the worker buffers until `response.body` is closed it would cause the silent window. Cloudflare docs mention `new Response(res.body)` is streaming, but some plugins or middlewares may fully buffer. Ask them to try `return new Response(res.body, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream' } })` explicitly and to avoid `.text()` or `.json()` on the response.
notes: Includes automated ops_bot message and actionable repro steps; customer confirmed worker path reproduces and direct path doesn't; team requested pcap/edge logs/request timestamps.
